messages.author: 29907bb1ee07b7e3
messages.subject: Tutorial issue - PDF plots
parts:
Hi, Nick!

I am teaching an introductory course in BioGeoBEARS here in Brazil this week and yesterday when the students and I were following the Example Script from your wiki page we came across an issue when trying to plot the DEC and DEC+J trees and create the PDF file containing them.
We are all running the latest version of R and RStudio in our computers.

All 4 trees with ancestral states are created just fine and we can see them in the Plots window in RStudio.
However, as we run the dev.off() command, all trees disappear from the Plot panel.
And, when we run the cmdstr = paste("open", pdffn, sep="") and system(cdmstr) commands, the pdf doesn't open. We get an error message that it cannot be opened.
When I go to the folder where files are being saved, I see that the PDF was created however it is just a 160 bytes only file that does not open.

This issue is happening in my macbook and my student's windows machines as well.

Hope you can help us, 
Vanessa Rivera.

messages.author: 29907bb1ee07b7e3
messages.subject: Re: Tutorial issue - PDF plots
parts:
Hey Nick, to give you a little bit more context:

Before we create the initial pdf call, on line 528 we have the following devices:

> dev.list()
        RStudioGD quartz_off_screen 
                2                 3 
> dev.cur()
RStudioGD 
        2

After we make the pdf call, a pdf device is created and set as the current device, as it should

> pdffn = "Psychotria_DEC_vs_DEC+J_M0_unconstrained_v1.pdf"
> pdf(pdffn, width=6, height=6)
> dev.list()
        RStudioGD quartz_off_screen               pdf 
                2                 3                 4 
> dev.cur()
pdf 
  4

But when we make the first call to plot_BioGeoBEARS_results it changes the current device back to RStudioinstead of being the pdf one, even though the pdf device still exists:

> dev.cur()
pdf 
  4 
> # States
> res2 = plot_BioGeoBEARS_results(results_object, analysis_titletxt, addl_params=list("j"), plotwhat="text", label.offset=0.45, tipcex=0.7, statecex=0.7, splitcex=0.6, titlecex=0.8, plotsplits=TRUE, cornercoords_loc=scriptdir, include_null_range=TRUE, tr=tr, tipranges=tipranges)
> dev.cur()
RStudioGD 
        2 
> dev.list()
        RStudioGD quartz_off_screen               pdf 
                2                 3                 4 
>

Because it changed the device to RStudioGD, now the other plots and the call to dev.off() will be operating on the wrong device, leaving you with an invalid pdf file.

We are running RStudio Version 1.1.453 and R:

> R.version
               _                           
platform       x86_64-apple-darwin17.5.0   
arch           x86_64                      
os             darwin17.5.0                
system         x86_64, darwin17.5.0        
status                                     
major          3                           
minor          5.0                         
year           2018                        
month          04                          
day            23                          
svn rev        74626                       
language       R                           
version.string R version 3.5.0 (2018-04-23)
nickname       Joy in Playing

Hope the extra information helps.

Thanks again,

Vanessa

messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Tutorial issue - PDF plots
parts: Hi - I have seen this happen occasionally but it’s nit very predictable- usually the solution is to run dev.off() several times to make sure all previous attempts and graphics windows and pdf writers are closed, and then run the pdf commands again. Cheers! Nixk
